source_text: Ἐγὼ δὲ εὖ οἶδα, ὡς οὔτε οἱ κουφότατοι δοκοῦντες τὸν μέγαν δρόμον ἐκεῖνον ἀνύσουσιν, οὔτε οἱ δυνατοὶ καὶ φοβεροὶ παρὰ ἀνθρώποις δεδοξασμένοι, τὸν φοβερὸν πόλεμον νικήσουσιν. Ἀλλ᾽ οὐδὲ ἐν ἐδωδῆς πλήθει φρόνησις δοκιμάζεται, οὐδὲ σύνεσις πλούτῳ κοινωνεῖν εἴωθεν. Οὐδὲ συγχαίρω τοῖς οἰομένοις ἅπαντας τῶν ὁμοίων τεύξεσθαι. Πάνυ δὲ ὑπνώττειν ἐοίκασιν οἱ τὰ τοιαῦτα ἐνθυμούμενοι, καὶ μὴ λογιζόμενοι, ὡς δίκην ἰχθύων καὶ ὀρνέων ἀνάρπαστοι γινόμενοι, ἐν κακοῖς κατατριβήσονται, ἄφνω τῆς ἀξίας λαχόντες ἐπιτιμίας. Ἐγὼ δὲ σοφίαν οὕτω τι μέγα ἡγοῦμαι, ὡς καὶ πόλιν μικρὰν ὑπ᾽ ὀλίγων μὲν οἰκουμένην, ὑπὸ δὲ μεγάλου πολιορκουμένην βασιλέως χειρὶ, πολλὴν καὶ μεγάλην ἡγοῦμαι, εἰ καὶ ἕνα σοφὸν ἄνδρα πολίτην ἔχοι πένητα. Δύναιτο γὰρ ἂν οὗτος καὶ ἐκ τῶν πολεμίων, καὶ ἐκ τῶν χαρακωμάτων τὴν ἑαυτοῦ διασῶσαι πόλιν. Καὶ ἄλλοι μὲν τὸν σοφὸν ἐκεῖνον οὐ γινώσκουσι πένητα· ἐγὼ δὲ καὶ πάνυ προκρίνω τὴν ἐν σοφίᾳ ἰσχὺν ταύτης τῆς δημώδους δυνάμεως. Ἀλλ᾽ ἐνθάδε μὲν ἀτιμάζεται σοφία πενίᾳ συνοικοῦσα· ἀκουσθήσεται δὲ μετέπειτα ὑπερφωνοῦσα δυνάστας καὶ τυράννους κακῶν ὀρεγομένους. Σοφία γὰρ καὶ σιδήρου δυνατωτέρα· Ἀφροσύνη τε ἑνὸς πολλοῖς κίνδυνον ἐργάζεται, κἂν πολλοῖς καταφρόνητος ᾖ.
thought_title: Wisdom surpasses strength and wealth; the poor wise man saves a city
orientation: Gregory, speaking in his own voice, rejects the self-indulgent advice of the "vain ones" from the previous passage and asserts that true wisdom outweighs speed, power, feasting, and riches, illustrating this with a parable of a poor wise man who delivers a besieged city.
pass_a_gloss: I myself know well that neither the swiftest runners who seem to complete that great race will finish it, nor will the powerful and fearsome men glorified among humans win the terrible war. Moreover, wisdom is not tested in an abundance of foods, nor is understanding accustomed to share in wealth. Nor do I rejoice with those who suppose they will attain all things like their peers. They seem altogether to be sleeping, those who ponder such things and do not reason that, like fish and birds snatched away, they will be worn down in evils, suddenly having obtained the penalty of their worth. I, however, esteem wisdom as something so great that even a small city inhabited by few, but besieged by the hand of a great king, I consider great and mighty, if it has even one wise man as a citizen, though poor. For this man could save his city both from the enemies and from the siege-works. And others do not know that wise poor man; but I myself greatly prefer the strength that is in wisdom over this common power. But here wisdom dwelling with poverty is dishonored; it will be heard afterward sounding above rulers and tyrants desiring evils. For wisdom is stronger than iron; and folly of one works danger for many, even if it is despised by many.

lemmas.gloss: I on the other hand / but I
I know well / I am fully aware
to be drowsy / to nod off / to be asleep
will be worn down / consumed / destroyed

choices.why: Metaphor for the course of life or the pursuit of worldly goals; literal rendering preserves the image.
Matches the context of feasting from the preceding passage; "foods" keeps the plural sense of ἐδωδῆς.

choices.english: they seem altogether to be sleeping
choices.why: Captures the force of ὑπνώττω (to be drowsy/nod off) + ἐοίκασιν (they seem); "altogether" renders Πάνυ.
Simile for sudden, helpless capture; δίκην governs the genitive.
rejected: in the manner of fish and birds

choices.english: the strength that is in wisdom
choices.why: Avoids reifying "wisdom's strength" as a compound; keeps the prepositional phrase explicit.
Ἀφροσύνη = folly (contrasted with σοφία); ἑνὸς = of one (person).

bible_refs.note: οὔτε τῶν κουφῶν ὁ δρόμος ... οὔτε τῶν δυνατῶν ὁ πόλεμος (LXX Eccl 9:11); source: οὔτε οἱ κουφότατοι ... ἀνύσουσιν, οὔτε οἱ δυνατοὶ ... νικήσουσιν

LXX Eccl 9:13-15: small city, few men, great king besieges, poor wise man delivers it; source: πόλιν μικρὰν ὑπ᾽ ὀλίγων ... ὑπὸ δὲ μεγάλου πολιορκουμένην βασιλέως χειρὶ ... ἕνα σοφὸν ἄνδρα πολίτην ἔχοι πένητα ... διασῶσαι πόλιν
LXX Eccl 9:16-17: wisdom better than strength, poor man's wisdom despised, words of wise heard in quiet; source: ἀτιμάζεται σοφία πενίᾳ συνοικοῦσα ... ἀκουσθήσεται δὲ μετέπειτα ὑπερφωνοῦσα δυνάστας
LXX Eccl 9:18: wisdom better than weapons of war, one sinner destroys much good; source: Σοφία γὰρ καὶ σιδήρου δυνατωτέρα ... Ἀφροσύνη τε ἑνὸς πολλοῖς κίνδυνον ἐργάζεται

pass_b_english: But I know full well that even the swiftest runners will not finish that great race, and those who are powerful and fearsome, renowned among men, will not win the terrible war. (Ecclesiastes 9:11 LXX) Wisdom is not tested by an abundance of foods, and understanding does not usually share in wealth. I do not rejoice with those who think that all people will obtain like outcomes. They seem altogether to be sleeping, those who ponder such things and do not reckon that, like fish and birds snatched away, they will be worn down in evils, suddenly receiving their due penalty. (Ecclesiastes 9:12 LXX) I consider wisdom so great a thing that if a small city, inhabited by few men but besieged by the hand of a great king, possessed even one wise citizen who was poor, I would count that city great and mighty. (Ecclesiastes 9:13-14 LXX) For such a man could save his city both from the enemy and from the siege works. (Ecclesiastes 9:15 LXX) Yet others do not recognize that poor wise man; but I greatly prefer the strength that is in wisdom over this common force. (Ecclesiastes 9:16 LXX) Here wisdom is dishonored because it dwells with poverty; but later it will be heard speaking louder than rulers and tyrants who desire evil things. (Ecclesiastes 9:17 LXX) For wisdom is stronger even than iron; and the folly of one person works danger for many, even if that folly is despised by many. (Ecclesiastes 9:18 LXX)

problems.quote: I do not rejoice with those who think they will obtain everything the same as everyone else.
problems.source_quote: Οὐδὲ συγχαίρω τοῖς οἰομένοις ἅπαντας τῶν ὁμοίων τεύξεσθαι.
problems.why: The source says all people will meet like outcomes (the same lot). The English adds 'everything' and is muddled, so it changes the claim and is hard to follow.
problems.fix: I do not rejoice with those who think that all people will obtain like outcomes.

edits.old: I do not rejoice with those who think they will obtain everything the same as everyone else.
edits.new: I do not rejoice with those who think that all people will obtain like outcomes.

fixed: Changed 'I do not rejoice with those who think they will obtain everything the same as everyone else.' to 'I do not rejoice with those who think that all people will obtain like outcomes.' Source: Οὐδὲ συγχαίρω τοῖς οἰομένοις ἅπαντας τῶν ὁμοίων τεύξεσθαι. The Greek means 'all (people) will obtain like/similar outcomes (τῶν ὁμοίων),' not 'obtain everything the same as everyone else.'
